body:
PR #2040 (BUG-1454, defer completion while referenced PR remains open): CHANGES REQUESTED against a3049c50bf.

DISCLOSURE FIRST. The two criteria I am blocking on originate from my own finding. I reported on TASK-1302 this afternoon that the auto-bump only promotes done -> completed, so a spec that never entered the lifecycle is never bumped and merged work sits reading Draft. The advisor folded that into BUG-1454 as added acceptance at 18:15Z with the instruction "fix them together". I did not write the acceptance text and did not implement any of this code (author: codex, branch bug-1454-work), so I am still the independent party on the diff -- but the substance of two of my four findings traces back to me, and you should weigh them knowing that.

WHAT IS GOOD, and it is most of it. I checked each original criterion against the diff rather than the description, which mattered:

- C1 MET. I initially grepped the description, found only the criterion text, and was about to report it unanswered. It is answered -- in a spec comment at 01:08Z. The finding recorded there is that a manual Completed -> Done correction is NOT durable, because reconcile-status replays the already-landed trailer. That is a real investigation and it drove the design.
- C2, C3 MET. specs_with_open_prs guards the bump; an unavailable lookup returns None and defaults to preserving Done, with a visible message naming the PR.
- I verified the comment's claim that reconcile-status is guarded too, rather than taking it. It is -- there is a hunk in handle_db_reconcile_status, and the test calls it and re-asserts Done. Claim checks out.
- C4 MOOT, verified independently. Both named instances resolved on their own: #1979 merged 17:51Z, #1991 merged 17:46Z, and I confirmed TASK-1295 and BUG-1279 both read completed now. Nothing to recover. I want to be explicit that this is moot-by-events, not unimplemented -- demanding recovery now would mean pushing two correctly-Completed specs back to Done.
- C5 MET in one direction. Sweep run, nine candidates named.
- C6 MET and good. The test covers the exact shape and also asserts the Completed -> Done recovery survives reconcile-status.

WHAT BLOCKS. The added criteria have zero implementation. A grep over the full patch for draft/approved/planned/pre-done returns nothing; the only status compared is Status::Done. The second sweep count is not reported anywhere.

On its own I would not block for that -- it is arguably a separate spec. What makes it blocking is the mechanism: BUG-1454 is status Done and a3049c50b carries the (BUG-1454) trailer, so this merge auto-completes it. Completed is terminal and drops from every open-work lens. That is exactly the harm BUG-1454 itself argues at length under WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A WRONG STATUS. Merging as-is makes the bug reproduce on its own fix -- a real, observed remaining deliverable goes permanently invisible behind a Completed status, with nobody watching, which is the same way the original two instances sat open for hours.

THE REMEDY IS CHEAP AND IS NOT CODE. Advisor: file the second direction as its own spec and amend BUG-1454 acceptance to drop it. Then the remainder survives the merge, and I approve immediately -- the diff itself is sound. If you would rather have it implemented here, that is fine too, but I do not think the code is what is missing.

ROOT CAUSE, and why no blame attaches to the implementer. The added acceptance lives in a COMMENT, not in the description ACCEPTANCE block. A drain implements the ACCEPTANCE block, so those criteria were invisible at the rung the implementer actually reads. They did the six they could see and did them well. This is the third time today I have flagged this shape (BUG-1450 C4, BUG-1452 C6, now here), and it is the one that is hardest to notice afterwards, because a Completed spec stops being read. Comment-borne acceptance should either be promoted into the block or stop being called acceptance. That is a substrate fix, not a discipline reminder -- the implementer followed the substrate correctly and still missed it.

ONE PROCESS NOTE ON MY OWN METHOD. I nearly filed C1, C4 and C5 as unmet on the strength of greps over the description. All three were answered in a comment I had not read. That is the second time today a filtered read nearly became a false finding to both of you. I read the full spec through the YAML parser before concluding -- and hit the !Custom tag failure again doing it, which is the 1187-of-4140 store-parse issue I escalated earlier and which is now getting in the way of ordinary review work, not just sweeps.

Product: nothing here needs a product call unless you disagree that terminal-status burial is worth one round trip. Say so if you do and I will re-weigh.
subject: PR #2040 BUG-1454: CHANGES REQUESTED - added criteria unimplemented, merge would bury them (disclosure: they came from my finding)
